nodes.label: Pokemon Red
nodes.description: A gameplay-feature map of the original Kanto RPG loop.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Pokemon Red is built around a repeated loop: explore Kanto, meet Pokemon and trainers, battle, capture or strengthen the team, then use new badges and abilities to unlock more of the world.

### Feature Perspective

This board treats the game as interconnected gameplay systems rather than as a plot summary. Each domain shows what the player does, what state changes, and how one system feeds another.

nodes.label: Exploration
nodes.description: Routes, towns, dungeons, NPCs, and hidden discoveries.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Exploration gives the player a readable overworld with towns, routes, caves, and optional secrets. Movement is simple, but the map is gated by battle progress, key items, and HM abilities.

nodes.label: Battles
nodes.description: Turn-based combat, moves, typing, status, and outcomes.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Battles are the primary challenge system. They combine team preparation with turn-by-turn decisions, making Pokemon identity, move choice, typing, and resource management matter.

nodes.label: Collection
nodes.description: Wild encounters, catching, Pokedex completion, party, and PC boxes.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Collection turns random encounters into long-term goals. Every route can offer new species, and the player balances a six-Pokemon party against the broader Pokedex and PC storage.

nodes.label: Progression
nodes.description: Experience, evolution, gyms, badges, HMs, and world access.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Progression links personal team growth to world structure. Pokemon level up and evolve, gyms certify mastery, and badges plus HMs open new routes through Kanto.

nodes.label: Economy & Recovery
nodes.description: Money, inventory, shops, Pokemon Centers, and field resources.
nodes.content:
## Overview

The economy makes exploration and battles durable over time. Items, money, healing, and storage let the player decide when to press deeper into a route and when to return to town.

nodes.label: Story & Gates
nodes.description: Rival fights, Team Rocket, key items, badge checks, and the Elite Four.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Story events are also gates. Rival battles, Team Rocket hideouts, key items, and the Pokemon League structure pace the player's access to harder challenges.

nodes.label: Explore, Battle, Grow
nodes.description: The core loop that moves the player from map discovery to team improvement.
nodes.content:
## Loop

1. Enter a new area.
2. Fight wild Pokemon or trainers.
3. Earn experience, money, and knowledge.
4. Heal, restock, and push farther.

This loop is short enough to repeat constantly but broad enough to support long-term goals.

nodes.label: Catch, Train, Counter
nodes.description: Collection and battle strategy reinforce one another.
nodes.content:
## Loop

The player catches Pokemon to expand tactical options, trains favorites to make them reliable, and changes the team to counter gyms, routes, and the Elite Four.

nodes.label: Gated Kanto
nodes.description: Badges, HMs, story flags, and key items reshape the traversable world.
nodes.content:
## Loop

Kanto feels open because earlier places remain relevant. New tools such as Cut, Surf, and Strength make old routes worth revisiting and turn progression into spatial knowledge.

nodes.label: Kanto Overworld
nodes.description: Grid-based towns, routes, caves, and buildings that host most play.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Presents Kanto as connected towns, routes, caves, and interiors
- Supports walking, tile collision, doors, ladders, ledges, and water traversal
- Hosts trainers, NPCs, hidden items, and environmental gates

nodes.label: Map Tile
nodes.description: A movement, collision, encounter, or interaction unit in the overworld.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Map tiles define where the player can walk, which terrain can trigger encounters, and which objects can be interacted with.

nodes.label: Route & Dungeon Design
nodes.description: Local layouts that shape risk, reward, and navigation pressure.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Mixes trainer placement, grass, shortcuts, puzzles, and item rewards
- Creates different rhythms for routes, caves, forests, towers, and water paths
- Teaches the player to prepare before long stretches without healing

nodes.label: Area Encounter Table
nodes.description: Species and level ranges available in grass, caves, or water.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Encounter tables give each area its collection identity. They make different routes useful even when the geometry is simple.

nodes.label: NPC Dialogue
nodes.description: Hints, jokes, trades, tutorials, and local flavor.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Teaches mechanics indirectly through townspeople and signs
- Offers optional trades and worldbuilding
- Points players toward gyms, HMs, and story blockers

nodes.label: Hidden Discovery
nodes.description: Optional items, secrets, and revisit rewards.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Rewards curiosity with hidden items and optional routes
- Makes backtracking valuable after new HMs
- Gives Kanto a sense of depth beyond the critical path

nodes.label: Turn-Based Battle
nodes.description: One-on-one Pokemon combat using commands, stats, moves, and switching.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Resolves player and opponent choices into turn order, damage, status, and fainting
- Lets players attack, use items, switch Pokemon, or run from wild battles
- Converts preparation into readable tactical decisions

nodes.label: Battle State
nodes.description: Active Pokemon, HP, status, stat modifiers, field context, and command choices.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Battle state tracks the current matchup and all temporary conditions needed to resolve the next turn.

nodes.label: Battle Outcome
nodes.description: Experience, money, fainting, capture chance, progression, or defeat.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Outcomes feed nearly every other domain: progression gains, money rewards, captured Pokemon, or a trip back to recovery.

nodes.label: Move System
nodes.description: Four move slots, PP, power, accuracy, type, and side effects.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Gives each Pokemon a limited tactical loadout
- Uses PP to add attrition across long routes and dungeons
- Provides personality through signature effects, accuracy risk, and status moves

nodes.label: Move
nodes.description: A battle command with type, PP, power, accuracy, and effects.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Moves are the core verbs of battle. A Pokemon's four move slots force tradeoffs between damage, coverage, utility, and endurance.

nodes.label: Type Matchups
nodes.description: Rock-paper-scissors-like damage multipliers across Pokemon and move types.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Rewards learning enemy weaknesses and resistances
- Encourages team diversity and move coverage
- Makes gym leaders feel distinct through type themes

nodes.label: Status Effects
nodes.description: Persistent or temporary conditions such as poison, paralysis, sleep, burn, and confusion.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Adds risk beyond raw HP damage
- Creates pressure to carry items or return to Pokemon Centers
- Enables low-level Pokemon and utility moves to matter

nodes.label: Wild Encounters
nodes.description: Random Pokemon battles triggered by terrain and area tables.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Turns exploration terrain into battle and collection opportunities
- Controls species availability by area
- Provides repeatable training and catching chances

nodes.label: Encounter State
nodes.description: The selected wild species, level, terrain, and battle context.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Encounter state bridges map exploration into a battle with a concrete wild Pokemon.

nodes.label: Catching
nodes.description: Poke Ball attempts based on species, HP, status, and ball type.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Converts battle advantage into collection progress
- Makes weakening and status effects useful outside winning
- Creates tension because balls, HP, and rare encounters are limited

nodes.label: Party Pokemon
nodes.description: A captured Pokemon with species, level, stats, moves, HP, and status.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Party Pokemon are both collectibles and playable characters. They carry long-term progression through levels, moves, and evolution.

nodes.label: Pokedex
nodes.description: Collection checklist and species encyclopedia.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Tracks seen and owned species
- Gives completion a visible goal
- Frames catching as discovery, not only team optimization

nodes.label: Pokedex Record
nodes.description: Seen or caught status plus species information.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Pokedex records turn encounters into durable collection knowledge, even when the player does not catch the Pokemon.

nodes.label: Party & PC Box
nodes.description: Six active Pokemon plus stored Pokemon managed through PCs.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Limits active choices to a six-Pokemon party
- Stores extra captures in PC boxes
- Makes team composition an ongoing strategic decision

nodes.label: Boxed Pokemon
nodes.description: Captured Pokemon stored outside the active party.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Boxed Pokemon preserve collection progress while keeping the moment-to-moment party readable.

nodes.label: Leveling & Evolution
nodes.description: Experience growth, stat increases, new moves, and species evolution.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Converts battles into lasting team power
- Rewards commitment to specific Pokemon
- Changes identity and capabilities through evolution and move learning

nodes.label: Experience Points
nodes.description: Growth currency awarded from battles.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Experience points are the main bridge from combat success to stronger Pokemon.

nodes.label: Gyms & Badges
nodes.description: Eight themed boss challenges that certify progress through Kanto.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Provides milestone battles with type-focused leaders
- Unlocks progression permissions such as obedience and HM use
- Structures the mid-game around regional mastery

nodes.label: Badge Set
nodes.description: The player's earned gym badges and related permissions.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Badges are compact progress state: they prove victory, unlock options, and gate the Pokemon League.

nodes.label: HM Abilities
nodes.description: Permanent field moves such as Cut, Fly, Surf, Strength, and Flash.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Lets battle moves double as world tools
- Opens old and new map paths after badge checks
- Connects team composition to exploration utility

nodes.label: HM Permission
nodes.description: Whether a field move can be used based on item ownership, badge ownership, and Pokemon compatibility.
nodes.content:
## Overview

HM permission is a progression gate that checks both inventory and earned badges before allowing field traversal.

nodes.label: Item Bag
nodes.description: Portable inventory for balls, medicine, key items, TMs, and battle tools.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Carries consumables and key items across the adventure
- Forces preparation through limited money and item quantities
- Links shops, battle recovery, catching, and puzzle progress

nodes.label: Inventory Item
nodes.description: A carried item with quantity, category, and usable contexts.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Inventory items are flexible tools: some heal, some capture, some teach moves, and some unlock story progress.

nodes.label: Poke Mart
nodes.description: Town shop that converts battle winnings into supplies.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Lets money become Poke Balls, potions, antidotes, repels, and other supplies
- Changes stock by location and progression
- Sets up planning before routes and dungeons

nodes.label: Money
nodes.description: Currency won from trainers and spent in shops.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Money connects trainer battles to preparation. Losing or overspending can make routes feel harder.

nodes.label: Pokemon Center
nodes.description: Free healing, PC access, and a rhythm reset point.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Restores party HP, PP, and major status conditions
- Anchors towns as safe hubs
- Supports team management through PC access

nodes.label: Rival Battles
nodes.description: Recurring team checks that mirror the player's journey.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Tests readiness at memorable route and dungeon moments
- Gives narrative personality to mechanical progress
- Foreshadows the final Champion fight

nodes.label: Team Rocket
nodes.description: Villain encounters that structure dungeons and key-item rewards.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Provides multi-battle story dungeons
- Awards key items and unlocks blocked city routes
- Varies the challenge beyond gyms and wild routes

nodes.label: Progression Gates
nodes.description: Checks for badges, key items, story flags, and HM capability.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Controls access to cities, routes, dungeons, and the Pokemon League
- Turns rewards into new navigation possibilities
- Keeps the adventure paced without a quest log

nodes.label: Story Flag
nodes.description: A hidden completion marker for events, blockers, and unlocks.
nodes.content:
## Overview

Story flags remember what the player has solved so the world can change: guards move, NPCs respond, and new paths become valid.

nodes.label: Elite Four & Champion
nodes.description: Endgame gauntlet that demands a complete, resilient team.
nodes.content:
## Responsibilities

- Requires all eight badges before entry
- Tests team depth across several high-level battles without normal recovery
- Converts the rival arc into the final Champion challenge
